### Local cache bypasses device limit after first rejection **High Severity** In `tagDeviceUI`, the local cache is populated *before* the `CreateOrUpdateDevice` DB call. When the device limit is reached and `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned, the cache entry remains. On subsequent requests from the same device (within the 29-minute cache TTL), the cache hit causes `tagDeviceUI` to return `nil`, so `Authenticate` succeeds — completely bypassing the device limit. A rejected anonymous user only needs to refresh the page to gain access.
Additional Locations (1) - [`pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go#L43-L46`](https://github.com/droid-code-review-evals/bugbot-grafana/blob/3647ba7360b8d157e4a294a650a365b6aca070d8/pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go#L43-L46)

### Duplicate constant across packages risks future inconsistency **Low Severity** `anonymousDeviceExpiration` is independently defined with the same value (`30 * 24 * time.Hour`) in both `database.go` and `api/api.go`. A third copy exists as `thirtyDays` in `impl.go`. These represent the same logical concept and risk diverging if only one is updated.
Additional Locations (1) - [`pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/api/api.go#L17-L18`](https://github.com/droid-code-review-evals/bugbot-grafana/blob/3647ba7360b8d157e4a294a650a365b6aca070d8/pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/api/api.go#L17-L18)

### Denial cache key collision due to ambiguous separator **Medium Severity** `userPermDenialCacheKey` concatenates `name` and `parent` using `_` as a separator, but Grafana UIDs explicitly allow underscores in their character set (`a-zA-Z0-9\-\_`). This creates ambiguous keys where different `(name, parent)` tuples produce identical cache keys — e.g., `(name="a_b", parent="c")` and `(name="a", parent="b_c")` both yield the suffix `"_a_b_c"`. A cached denial for one resource would incorrectly deny a different resource. Additionally, since `permDenialCache` and `permCache` share the same underlying `cache.Cache` instance, the denial key prefix overlaps with the permission key prefix, which could cause cross-type cache corruption.
Additional Locations (1) - [`pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go#L115-L121`](https://github.com/droid-code-review-evals/bugbot-grafana/blob/d9dc93c4a6c88ef850dbe526cb3226ae99cafa20/pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go#L115-L121)

prs.title: Plugins: Chore: Renamed instrumentation middleware to metrics middleware

review_comments.body:
### `TestLogger.FromContext` returns disconnected logger, losing log calls **Medium Severity** `TestLogger.FromContext` returns a brand new `NewTestLogger()` that is completely disconnected from the original instance. Since `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` now calls `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`, the `Info` call goes to this ephemeral logger that is immediately discarded. Any test verifying log output via the original `TestLogger`'s `InfoLogs.Calls` or `InfoLogs.Message` fields will see zero calls, silently hiding logging regressions. `FromContext` likely needs to return `f` (the receiver) instead.
Additional Locations (1) - [`pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/logger_middleware.go#L57-L58`](https://github.com/droid-code-review-evals/bugbot-grafana/blob/00393c2ac9103072bc2194118e455f9248a37816/pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/logger_middleware.go#L57-L58)

### Double interpolation causes duplicate ad hoc filters **High Severity** When shard splitting is active, `applyTemplateVariables` is called twice on the same queries — first in `runShardSplitQuery` and then again when `splitQueriesByStreamShard` delegates to `runSplitQuery`. The `applyTemplateVariables` method calls `addAdHocFilters`, which unconditionally appends ad hoc filter labels via `addLabelToQuery` without checking for duplicates. This causes ad hoc filters to appear twice in the final query sent to Loki.
Additional Locations (2) - [`public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/shardQuerySplitting.ts#L48-L52`](https://github.com/droid-code-review-evals/bugbot-grafana/blob/3ba2457a7090b2b76f4b368c8a9db835d0bec66c/public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/shardQuerySplitting.ts#L48-L52) - [`public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/shardQuerySplitting.ts#L162-L163`](https://github.com/droid-code-review-evals/bugbot-grafana/blob/3ba2457a7090b2b76f4b368c8a9db835d0bec66c/public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/shardQuerySplitting.ts#L162-L163)

### Non-shard split queries also get double interpolation **High Severity** Even without shard splitting, the new `applyTemplateVariables` call in `runSplitQuery` causes double interpolation because `DataSourceWithBackend.query()` (called via `datasource.runQuery` → `super.query()`) also calls `applyTemplateVariables` on every target. This means ad hoc filters from `addAdHocFilters` are appended twice to every time-split query, not just shard-split ones. Before this change, `runSplitQuery` did not interpolate, so `DataSourceWithBackend.query()` was the sole interpolation point.

### Missing `key` prop for GrafanaRuleListItem in list map **Medium Severity** The `GrafanaRuleListItem` in the `'grafana'` case is missing the `key={key}` prop, while both the `'datasource'` and `default` cases correctly pass it. The `key` variable is destructured from `ruleWithOrigin` on the line above and is available. Without it, React falls back to array indices for reconciliation, which can cause incorrect UI updates (stale state, wrong items rendered) when the filtered rule list changes.

### Recording rules lose abilities due to alerting-only check **Medium Severity** In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, `isAlertingRule` is set via `prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`, which is `true` only for alerting rules. It's then used for `ModifyExport`, `Pause`, `Restore`, and `DeletePermanently`. However, the equivalent in `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` uses `isGrafanaManagedAlertRule = rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`, which matches *all* Grafana rules (alerting and recording). This means Grafana recording rules lose export, pause, restore, and permanent-delete capabilities when accessed through the prom-based code path (i.e., the list view).

### Silence drawer never opens in prom-only path **High Severity** When `GrafanaRuleListItem` renders `RuleActionsButtons` it only passes `promRule`, leaving `rule` (the `RulerRuleDTO`) as `undefined`. The "Silence notifications" menu item correctly appears via `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, and clicking it sets `showSilenceDrawer` to `true`. However, the `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` is guarded by `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`, which is always `false` when `rule` is `undefined`. The drawer never opens — the button is visible but silently does nothing.
Additional Locations (1) - [`public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx#L46-L47`](https://github.com/droid-code-review-evals/bugbot-grafana/blob/3e6d620d2c1d1f6c10611fba8b0ee062d6fb2a68/public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx#L46-L47)

### Storage error records legacy duration metric instead **Medium Severity** When `d.Storage.Create` fails, `recordLegacyDuration` is called instead of `recordStorageDuration`. The same mistake occurs in `Update` on the storage error path. This causes storage operation failures to be incorrectly attributed to the legacy metric, corrupting both the `dual_writer_legacy_duration_seconds` and `dual_writer_storage_duration_seconds` metrics. Comparing with `dualwriter_mode2.go`, storage errors consistently use `recordStorageDuration`.
Additional Locations (1) - [`pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go#L128-L129`](https://github.com/droid-code-review-evals/bugbot-grafana/blob/67b74e1e8a7d26d24617b7313b90fa4649138318/pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go#L128-L129)

### Delete passes object name instead of Kind to metrics **Medium Severity** On the success path of `Delete`, `recordStorageDuration` receives `name` (the object name, e.g. "foo") as the third argument instead of `options.Kind`. The error path on line 103 correctly passes `options.Kind`. This creates inconsistent and incorrect metric labels — high-cardinality object names will pollute the `kind` dimension of the histogram.

### DeleteCollection goroutine records storage instead of legacy duration **Medium Severity** Inside the `DeleteCollection` goroutine, the legacy `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection` result is recorded via `d.recordStorageDuration` instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration`. This misattributes legacy operation timings to the storage metric. All other goroutines doing legacy writes in this file correctly use `recordLegacyDuration`.

### Delete context uses base logger missing enriched values **Low Severity** In `Delete`, the context is set with `klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` using the base logger, while the local `log` variable on line 96 was enriched with `name`, `kind`, and `method` values. Every other method in this file correctly passes the enriched `log` to `klog.NewContext`. This means downstream code extracting the logger from context won't see those useful values.

### Debug-level logging accidentally uses Error log level **High Severity** All six new `r.log.Error` calls in `CleanAnnotations` and `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags` log routine operational information (e.g. "Annotations to clean by time", "cleaned annotations by time") at `Error` level. These are clearly debug statements that were left in. In production, every cleanup cycle will emit multiple error-level log entries with potentially huge `ids` slices (up to batch-size elements), polluting error logs, likely triggering alerting, and degrading log readability. Additionally, on lines 534 and 554, the logged `err` is always `nil` at that point.
Additional Locations (2) - [`pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go#L553-L557`](https://github.com/droid-code-review-evals/bugbot-grafana/blob/81c45bfe449584dc7ff50e4fabd5d0c6568999b5/pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go#L553-L557) - [`pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go#L575-L579`](https://github.com/droid-code-review-evals/bugbot-grafana/blob/81c45bfe449584dc7ff50e4fabd5d0c6568999b5/pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go#L575-L579)

### Cleanup ticker interval reduced from 10 to 1 minute **Medium Severity** The `CleanUpService.Run` ticker was changed from `time.Minute * 10` to `time.Minute * 1`, increasing the cleanup frequency by 10x. This appears to be a debug/testing change that was accidentally included. The `clean` function's 9-minute timeout was designed around the original 10-minute interval. Running every minute adds unnecessary database load — counterproductive for a "Database Performance Optimizations" PR.

### Missing double-check after acquiring write lock **Medium Severity** The classic double-checked locking pattern is incomplete. After acquiring the write lock, `entryPointAssetsCache` isn't re-checked for nil. Multiple goroutines can pass the `ret != nil` check concurrently, then queue on the write lock — each one will redundantly re-read the manifest from disk or CDN instead of using the value already computed by the first goroutine. This causes a thundering-herd of redundant I/O on startup under concurrent requests while the write lock is held.

### Feature flag function always returns false **High Severity** `enableSqlExpressions` always returns `false` due to two compounding errors. First, the feature flag check is negated (`!h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(...)`) so `enabled` is `true` when the flag is *off*. Second, both the `if enabled` branch and the fallthrough return `false`, making the result unconditionally `false`. SQL expressions will always be rejected with "not implemented" regardless of the feature flag state.

### Context and goroutine leak when Init fails **Medium Severity** When `s.Init(ctx)` fails, `NewResourceServer` returns `nil, err` without calling `cancel()` on the context created at line 229. Since the server object `s` is not returned to the caller, `Stop()` can never be called and the `cancel` function becomes unreachable. This leaks the context (parented on `context.Background()`, so never auto-cancelled). Worse, if `search.init` partially succeeds before `initWatcher` fails, the search watcher goroutine (started with `context.Background()`) will also leak permanently.
Additional Locations (1) - [`pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go#L228-L248`](https://github.com/droid-code-review-evals/bugbot-grafana/blob/d762a9643618a6ba7c43da27374bd9ffc80889ce/pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go#L228-L248)
